accepted.s: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature primarily because he
o: composed the first Telugu literary work, Andhra Mahabharatamu
founded the first Telugu literary academy at Vengi
translated the complete Ramayana into Telugu
introduced the prose style into Sanskrit literature
accepted.x: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as Adi Kavi because Andhra Mahabharatamu is considered the first major Telugu literary work.
accepted.tq: Use the exact title and achievement associated with the poet.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the portion of the Mahabharata rendered by Nannaya in Telugu?
o: The Adi, Sabha and part of the Aranya parvas
Only the Udyoga and Bhishma parvas
The Sabha, Virata and Drona parvas
accepted.x: Nannaya rendered approximately two and a half parvas: Adi, Sabha and a portion of Aranya.
accepted.tq: Test the extent of a literary work through a precise list-based option.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Andhra Mahabharatamu of Nannaya is written in which literary style?
o: Champu style combining verse and prose
accepted.x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu follows the Champu style, which combines verse and prose.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related literary forms by identifying the defining feature.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Nannaya Bhattaraka?
accepted.x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was the title of Narayana Bhattu. Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.
accepted.tq: Find the title belonging to the collaborator rather than the principal poet.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Andhra Shabda Chintamani, associated with Nannaya, is best described as a work on
accepted.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani is a Sanskrit grammatical work dealing with Telugu grammar.
accepted.tq: Match the work with its subject and language rather than with the author's better-known epic.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Narayana Bhattu, the collaborator of Nannaya, was known by which title?
accepted.x: Narayana Bhattu bore the title Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara. The other titles are associated with Nannaya or Eastern Chalukya rulers.
accepted.tq: Use a person–title association and avoid the famous-word substitution trap.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.x: Ugradityacharya authored Kalyanakaraka, a medical treatise. Kavijanasrayam was associated with Vemulavada Bhimakavi, while Pavuluri Ganitamu was by Pavuluri Mallana.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: The earliest Telugu inscription mentioned in connection with the pre-Nannaya period is the
accepted.x: The Kalamalla inscription, dated approximately to 575 CE and associated with Renati Choda Dhananjaya, predates Nannaya.
accepted.tq: Use the earliest-date clue to distinguish inscriptions from different periods.
accepted.sec: Nannaya and other Telugu figures → patron + collaborator

accepted.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
accepted.x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.
accepted.tq: Test an unusual person–grant association, a common source of identity traps.
accepted.sec: Queens and Jain patronage (Nedumba Vasati, Ayyana Mahadevi, Potla Cheruvu)

accepted.s: Potla Cheruvu was known during the Eastern Chalukya period as a centre of
accepted.x: Potla Cheruvu was a popular Jain centre during this period.
accepted.tq: Identify the religious association of a place rather than its location alone.
accepted.sec: Queens and Jain patronage (Nedumba Vasati, Ayyana Mahadevi, Potla Cheruvu)

accepted.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have granted Mushikonda to the Jains?
accepted.x: Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda to the Jains, illustrating the dynasty's religious tolerance.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–religious patronage association without confusing it with temple construction.
accepted.sec: Queens and Jain patronage (Nedumba Vasati, Ayyana Mahadevi, Potla Cheruvu)

accepted.s: Kundavva, who became the queen of Vimaladitya, was the mother of
accepted.x: Kundavva was a Chola princess and the queen of Vimaladitya; she was the mother of Rajaraja Narendra.
accepted.tq: Trace the family relationship instead of confusing a queen with a ruler.
accepted.sec: Queens and Jain patronage (Nedumba Vasati, Ayyana Mahadevi, Potla Cheruvu)

accepted.s: The use of the matronymic ‘Hariti-putra’ by the Eastern Chalukyas is comparable to its use by the
accepted.x: The matronymic Hariti-putra was also used by the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas, indicating a southern cultural connection.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison group stated with the distinctive title or matronymic.
accepted.sec: Official language, religious sect favoured, mother goddess

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kushmandini was the mother goddess worshipped by the early Chalukyas. Hariti-putra is a matronymic, while the other two pairs confuse unrelated terms.
accepted.tq: Separate a deity name from a dynastic title, text and place name.
accepted.sec: Official language, religious sect favoured, mother goddess

accepted.s: Who among the following developed Kandukuru as another ‘Bejawada’?
o: Vijayaditya III, also known as Gunaga Vijayaditya
accepted.x: Vijayaditya III, or Gunaga Vijayaditya, developed Kandukuru as another Bejawada.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ruler associated with town development from rulers linked with capitals.
accepted.sec: Court titles and towns developed → person (Gandharva-vidya-visarada, Kandukuru → Bejawada)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the early capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas is correct?
o: Pithapuram was the first capital under Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
Rajamahendravaram was the first capital under Jayasimha Vallabha I.
Vijayawada was the first capital under Amma I.
Vengi was the first capital under Rajaraja Narendra.
accepted.x: Pithapuram, or Pishtapura, was the first capital under Kubja Vishnuvardhana. Vengi was adopted later, and Rajamahendravaram was subsequently important as a capital.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘first capital’ clue to distinguish initial and later seats of power.
accepted.sec: Court titles and towns developed → person (Gandharva-vidya-visarada, Kandukuru → Bejawada)

accepted.s: The capital of the Eastern Chalukyas was shifted to Vengi by
accepted.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.
accepted.tq: Match a capital change with the ruler responsible for it.
accepted.sec: Court titles and towns developed → person (Gandharva-vidya-visarada, Kandukuru → Bejawada)

accepted.s: The Magallu inscription is significant in Andhra history because it is regarded as the first inscription to mention the
accepted.x: The Magallu inscription is noted as the first inscription mentioning the Kakatiyas.
accepted.tq: Identify the dynasty connected with a landmark inscription rather than the dynasty ruling at the time.

accepted.s: Which of the following chronological periods is correctly matched with the dynasty or political phase?
accepted.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled approximately from 624 to 1075 CE. The other periods belong respectively to the Chalukya-Chola phase, Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara.
accepted.tq: Check the date range against the dynasty before accepting the sequence-related option.
